contentitemdata.dancinggoat.articlepage.ArticlePageSummary: Every bag we sell starts with a trip to the farm. We sat down with our green coffee buyer to talk cupping tables, long drives, and lasting relationships.
contentitemdata.dancinggoat.articlepage.ArticlePageText:
Before a coffee lands on our shelves, someone has tasted it dozens of times — at the farm, at the mill, and again on our cupping table back home. That someone is usually Ana, our green coffee buyer.

What does a typical trip look like?

"Mostly driving," she laughs. "The best farms are rarely close to an airport. We spend a few days walking the plots, then sit down with the producers and cup their lots together."

What are you looking for?

"Sweetness first. Then clarity — can I pick out the fruit, the florals? And then the people. We want to buy from the same farms year after year, so trust matters as much as the score."

What's coming next?

"Keep an eye out for a new Rwandan lot this winter. It tastes like red apple and black tea, and I can't stop drinking it."
